answer: Sybils are cheap to mint, costly to keep. Each agent must periodically prove it still holds a fragment of its own older state — a signed relic from an epoch in which it was witnessed — and pass that digest to a neighbour, who forwards a whisper of it onward. Bulk identities share one blank genesis, so a farm folds into a single vertex: every puppet returns the same fragment and the divergence check fails at once. Passing takes an unbroken chain of custody, which puts an upkeep cost in uptime and storage on each account, long before it earns. Forging that history costs more than the accounts.
